chunks: It is narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam that he said:
I used to sell Sabiri cloth in the shade, and Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام passed by me while riding. He said to me, 'O Hisham, selling in the shade is deceit, and deceit is not permissible.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ: Abu al-Hasan the First, a title of Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام
key_terms.السَّابِرِيَّ: Sabiri cloth, a type of fabric being sold
key_terms.الظِّلَالِ: the shade, where the goods were being sold in a way that could obscure their condition
key_terms.غِشٌّ: deceit or fraudulent dealing in commerce
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: is not permissible in the Shariah

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام forbid selling in the shade?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام forbade selling goods in a way that conceals their true condition from the buyer. It teaches that commercial dealings must be conducted with honesty and transparency, and that deceit in trade is haram.
